html:
The Trump administration today initiated sweeping changes to US public health policy, signing an executive order to limit childhood vaccines and recommending against several routine shots for children, challenging the authority of the CDC. This comes as the administration's efforts to end the war with Iran and reopen the Strait of Hormuz appear to have stalled, leading to intensified rhetoric and military changes in Tehran.

US Policy & Administration: Trump signed an executive order to split the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine and override the CDC's schedule, also recommending against hepatitis b, Covid-19, and influenza shots for children. RFK Jr., the health secretary, and Trump reportedly referenced autism during the signing. Separately, Todd Blanche, Trump’s former personal lawyer, was sworn in as US attorney general. Greenland also issued a sharp rebuke to a Trump-linked oil company for moving drilling equipment ashore without approval.

Middle East Tensions & Diplomacy: Negotiations to end the war with Iran and reopen the Strait of Hormuz have stalled. Trump demands Iran pay compensation for US soldier deaths and its own civilians, while Iran has its own conditions for reopening the Strait, stating it will not do so without the US meeting all demands. Iran appointed Mohsen Rezaei as its top security official and representative of Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. Amidst these tensions, Iran reportedly fired cruise missiles at an ADNOC tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, setting it ablaze, and Iran-backed Houthis struck Yemen's Red Sea port of Mocha. Oil prices are rising due to uncertainty. Separately, Prime Minister Netanyahu has rejected a 15-point plan proposed by Trump for Gaza, and an understanding has been reached between the US, Israel, Syria, and the IAEA to neutralize a secret Syrian nuclear site, 'Site 99'.

Global Security & Russia-Ukraine: A new joint defense agreement, the Mecca Pact, has been signed by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan, with observers suggesting its aim is to prevent Iran and Israel from regional dominance. Egypt reportedly refused to join. In Russia, the only liberal, anti-war party, Yabloko, was barred from parliamentary elections. Russia and Ukraine continue deep cross-border air attacks, with a Ukrainian drone attack on Nizhnekamsk killing 12. Syria and Russia also reached a deal on the future of the Tartous and Hmeimim bases.

Global Economy & Social Issues: The Reserve Bank of Australia is predicted to hold its cash rate at 4.35%. Iran's war-intensified economic crisis is causing household budgets to shrink, with reports of declining dairy and red meat consumption and millions facing poverty. ASEAN governments are seeking a joint strategy to combat cyberscams. In social developments, protests over exam leaks continue in India, and Malaysia is seeing increased tensions and evictions for Rohingya refugees due to hate speech.

Natural Disasters & Health: A powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake in Colombia has caused over 100 deaths and the collapse of dozens of buildings, trapping people in cities like Cali. In Asia, Typhoon Dolphin forced over 1 million people to evacuate on China's eastern coast, while monsoon rains in India's Assam region caused floods that have killed 100 people. Canada's Okanagan region is grappling with wildfires leading to over 12,000 evacuations and home losses. Concerns are also rising over a fast-moving Ebola outbreak in DR Congo, which the WHO warns is ahead of authorities.
